turning-lg-gallows: When a corrupt magistrate ordered an innocent hanged, {firstName} stood at the foot of the gallows and refused to move. Since that day, {{he|she|they}} {{has|has|have}} served the law only where it serves justice.
turning-lg-bridge: {firstName} once held a bridge without help so that a whole village could flee. The scars remain, and so does a promise to protect those who cannot protect themselves.
turning-lg-order: After watching a city sink into chaos, {firstName} swore to uphold order and mercy together, convinced that one without the other is a kind of cruelty.
turning-ng-plague: During the Grey Plague, when everyone else fled, {firstName} stayed to care for the sick without asking who they were. Laws and lords matter little to {{him|her|them}}; people matter a great deal.
turning-ng-market: {firstName} once spent a small fortune buying the freedom of children sold at a market, and would do it again tomorrow.
turning-ng-stranger: A stranger once saved {firstName}'s life and asked nothing in return. Ever since, {firstName} has tried to pass that kindness on, whatever the cost.
turning-cg-taxes: When the baron raised taxes for a war nobody wanted, {firstName} raided his tax wagons and gave the silver back to the villages. A bounty followed, and a reputation.
turning-cg-prison: {firstName} broke a friend out of a prison where her only crime had been singing the wrong song. To {firstName}, a rule that crushes people is an invitation to break it.
turning-cg-chains: Freedom has come first for {firstName} ever since a stolen axe was enough to break the chains of a slave caravan.
turning-ln-contract: To {firstName}, a given word is worth more than gold: {{he|she|they}} once completed a contract for an employer who had died, simply because a promise had been made.
turning-ln-court: Years of serving a court taught {firstName} that the law is imperfect but necessary. Without rules, the strong simply devour the weak.
turning-ln-collapse: {firstName} has seen what happens when order collapses, and has chosen a side: the side of rules, whoever wrote them.
turning-tn-balance: A druid once told {firstName} that every fire needs ash and every flood needs drought. Since then, {{he|she|they}} {{has|has|have}} tried to keep that balance.
turning-tn-survive: Wars, kings and prophets come and go; {firstName} has learned to keep {{his|her|their}} head down and look after {{his|her|their}} own.
turning-tn-wander: {firstName} refuses to take sides in quarrels that are not {{his|hers|theirs}}, preferring to watch, learn and move on.
turning-cn-banquet: {firstName} lives by one simple rule: no rules. {{He|She|They}} once left a royal banquet through a window because the music was boring.
turning-cn-cage: After years in a cage, {firstName} swore never to belong to anyone again: not to a lord, nor a guild, nor a cause.
turning-cn-dice: {firstName} once bet a ship on a single roll of the dice, and won. Since then, chance has felt more trustworthy than any king.
turning-le-ladder: {firstName} learned that the law is a ladder for those clever enough to climb it, and has been climbing ever since, stepping on whoever stands in the way.
turning-le-warlord: In the service of a ruthless warlord, {firstName} came to admire his methods: order through fear, loyalty through debt.
turning-le-letter: {firstName} keeps every promise to the letter, and writes promises so that the letter always favours {{him|her|them}}.
turning-ne-purse: A single purse of gold, stolen from a dying man, taught {firstName} that the world rewards those who take. {{He|She|They}} {{has|has|have}} been taking ever since.
turning-ne-betrayal: Betrayed by {{his|her|their}} closest friend, {firstName} decided never to trust anyone again, and to use others before they could do the same.
turning-ne-power: {firstName} cares for neither law nor freedom, only for power, and measures every friendship by what it can bring.
turning-ce-fire: The day {firstName} set fire to the house where {{he|she|they}} had been mistreated, something broke for good. Since then, destruction has tasted like freedom.
turning-ce-topple: {firstName} delights in watching order collapse, and has already toppled a mayor, a guild and a temple just to see what would happen.
turning-ce-shrine: Whispers from a forbidden shrine promised {firstName} power without limits. The price was mercy, and {{he|she|they}} paid it gladly.
turning-lg-witness: {firstName} once testified against a powerful lord before the royal court, knowing it would cost everything. The lord fell; so did {firstName}'s fortune, but not {{his|her|their}} pride.
turning-lg-plague-ward: During a plague, {firstName} enforced the quarantine that saved a city, and stayed inside the walls with the sick until the very end.
turning-ng-flood: When the river flooded, {firstName} spent three days rowing between rooftops, and has never since been able to walk past someone in need.
turning-ng-thief: {firstName} once caught a starving child stealing bread, paid the baker, and shared the meal; that child now writes letters every winter.
turning-cg-mine: {firstName} led a revolt of miners against a cruel overseer, then burned the debt ledgers so that no one could ever claim them again.
turning-cg-wedding: {firstName} once stopped a forced wedding by stealing the bride away on the bride's own horse, and has been wanted in three baronies ever since.
turning-ln-ledger: Working as a tax clerk, {firstName} found a single wrong number in the king's ledgers and refused to let it go, whatever the consequences.
turning-ln-oath: {firstName} swore an oath to a dying captain and kept it for ten years, even after learning that the captain had lied about everything.
turning-tn-river: After years of fighting other people's wars, {firstName} sat by a river for a whole season and came back with the conviction that no side is ever entirely right.
turning-tn-trade: {firstName} has worked for kings and for bandits, and judges both by the same rule: a deal is a deal.
turning-cn-heist: {firstName} once stole a crown just to see whether it could be done, and gave it back the next day for the same reason.
turning-cn-prophecy: A seer foretold {firstName}'s entire life in detail, so {{he has|she has|they have}} been doing the exact opposite ever since, out of principle.
turning-le-guild: {firstName} climbed the ranks of the merchants' guild by following every rule to the letter, and using those rules to ruin every rival.
turning-le-inquisitor: {firstName} served as an inquisitor and found that fear makes people obey far better than faith ever did.
turning-ne-poison: {firstName} inherited a fortune after a sudden illness struck an uncle. The healers never understood it; {firstName} never explained it.
turning-ne-informer: {firstName} discovered that secrets sell better than swords, and has kept a little book of other people's sins ever since.
turning-ce-riot: {firstName} started a riot in a city square just to cover a small theft, and found that watching the chaos was the better reward.
turning-ce-pact: {firstName} made a pact with something that whispers in the dark, and has never once regretted the price, which others pay.
